name: Traumatic Neuroma
definition: Disorganized regenerative nerve tissue forming after nerve injury or transection, potentially causing focal neuropathic pain and Tinel-positive tenderness.

typical: Focal electric/shooting pain at prior injury site

investigations.principle: Ultrasound and MRI can demonstrate neuroma and exclude other masses.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, marrow, infection, occult injury or other condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific diagnostic pathway.

amber: Persistent disabling neuroma may require targeted nerve surgery.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Vata-neuralgic phenotype may be documented descriptively.

patientEducation.summary: Disorganized regenerative nerve tissue forming after nerve injury or transection, potentially causing focal neuropathic pain and Tinel-positive tenderness.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute neurovascular compromise, major trauma, rapidly progressive weakness, suspected serious infection, sepsis, pathological instability or other listed red flags.
